name: Congenital Anomaly of the Tricuspid Valve Chordae

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Tricuspid Valve Anomaly Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Echocardiographic evidence of abnormal or malformed tricuspid valve chordae tendineae
Presence of clinical signs consistent with tricuspid regurgitation such as holosystolic murmur at lower left sternal border
Exclusion of other structural cardiac anomalies that could explain symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic confirmation of chordae anomaly plus clinical signs of tricuspid regurgitation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging and clinical correlation; genetic testing may be considered if syndromic features present.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Holosystolic murmur at lower left sternal border
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic murmur due to tricuspid regurgitation
searchTerms: heart murmur throughout systole at lower left chest
continuous murmur at left lower chest

pathognomonic.symptomName: Echocardiographic visualization of malformed tricuspid valve chordae tendineae
pathognomonic.notes: Direct imaging evidence diagnostic of anomaly
searchTerms: echocardiogram showing malformed heart valve cords
abnormal tricuspid valve tendons on echo
malformed valve chordae on heart ultrasound

common.notes: Secondary to volume overload from regurgitation
Indicative of elevated right atrial pressure

occasional.notes: Congestive hepatomegaly secondary to right heart failure
Occasional arrhythmias related to atrial enlargement

rare.notes: Due to arrhythmia or low cardiac output
In cases with associated shunts or severe regurgitation
Rare complication secondary to atrial enlargement and arrhythmias

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible elevated liver enzymes in congestive hepatopathy
imaging: Echocardiography showing malformed or shortened tricuspid valve chordae tendineae
Right atrial enlargement on chest X-ray
Cardiac MRI for detailed valve and chordae anatomy
genetic: No specific gene identified; may be associated with syndromic congenital heart diseases
other: Electrocardiogram showing right atrial enlargement or arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets
Presence of vegetations on valve leaflets

redFlags: Severe tricuspid regurgitation with right heart failure
Progressive hepatomegaly and ascites indicating congestive hepatopathy
references: Orphanet: Congenital anomaly of the tricuspid valve chordae (ORPHA:99055)
Moss & Adams' Heart Disease in Infants, Children, and Adolescents, 9th Edition
Echocardiographic assessment of congenital tricuspid valve anomalies - Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography, 2022
